links.outcome: Alignment of LLM orthopaedic treatment choices with most popular surgeon responses on real cases
links.effect: Most-popular-response agreement: ChatGPT 4 68.0%, ChatGPT 3.5 40.2%, Bard 45.4% (P<0.001); poorer on controversial questions.
links.quote: ChatGPT 4 demonstrated the highest proportion of most popular responses (proportion of most popular response: ChatGPT 4 68.0%, ChatGPT 3.5 40.2%, Bard 45.4%, P value < 0.001), outperforming other AI tools.

links.outcome: Consistency of responses across AI tools and repeated use
links.effect: Inter-tool Cohen's kappa ranged from 0.201 (ChatGPT 4 vs. Bard) to 0.634 (ChatGPT 3.5 vs. Bard); responses varied widely.
links.quote: However, AI tool responses varied widely, reflecting a need for consistency in real-world clinical applications.

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates the performance of ChatGPT 3.5, ChatGPT 4, and Google Bard on answering orthopaedic clinical decision-making vignettes from OrthoBullets compared to human clinician consensus. It evaluates model accuracy alone without testing a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
